proposal.summary: CM550's J1939 start-up (mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink) builds the transmit descriptors and then schedules 19 periodic broadcasts with 0x1fe84. 0x1fe84 is the twin of CM848's scheduler 0x538c8c. Each 10-byte queue entry holds the PGN key, the interval and next send in 10 ms ticks, and the builder's address, and cm550_runJ1939PeriodicTransmitQueues calls the builder when its tick comes. CM848 does not send PGN 65252 SHUTDN. In CM550, 0x33dfa builds its descriptor, and 0x33d38 fills payload bytes 1-4 (idle shutdown state, idle shutdown enable, A/C pressure switch, wait to start lamp) and sends it, both every 1000 ms and as the responder to a PGN 59904 request. The rows tsc1_message_* (0x801d44 / 0x801d48) are ETC1 bytes 1 and 5 kept by the ETC1 receive handler 0x2efd0; the real TSC1 bytes are at 0x801d4c-0x801d58. DGFUIDEN (0x806abc, 19 words) is a per-fault processing enable bitmap that every reader ANDs with the same bit of the system error status words at 0x806000. The four 2D lookup functions are the start-up initializer and the periodic lookup for two values: the maximum torque at the current engine speed (MTMPRPFL) and the injection timing misfire limit (BSTAMNLM).

functions.role: Adds one periodic J1939 broadcast (PGN key, interval, first-send offset, builder address) to transmit queue 0 (20 entries) or queue 1 (10 entries) and returns 1 when the queue is full.
functions.discriminator: It is the only writer of the periodic queues (entries 0x80096e / 0x800a36, counts 0x800a9a / 0x800a9b): it converts the interval and the offset from ms to 10 ms ticks and adds the queue's current tick to the offset. cm550_runJ1939PeriodicTransmitQueues only reads the entries and calls the builders.
functions.plate_comment: Adds a periodic J1939 broadcast to transmit queue 0 (the engine node: 20 entries of 10 bytes at 0x80096e) or queue 1 (the retarder node: 10 entries at 0x800a36): the PGN key, the interval in ms kept as 10 ms ticks, the first send as the queue's current tick plus the offset in ticks, and the builder's address. Returns 1 when the queue is full, else 0. mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink schedules the 19 broadcasts with it (the first is PGN 65265 every 100 ms from 70 ms) and cm550_runJ1939PeriodicTransmitQueues calls each builder when its tick comes. The twin of CM848 0x538c8c: one shared name (no row before; PR #53 round 94)
functions.evidence: CM550 0x1fe84-0x1ff36: a3 = 0x800a9a, a1 = 0x800a9b; move.l (0x10,a7) is the queue. Queue 0: cmpi.b #0x14,(a3) (full: moveq #1 / rts), entry = count++ x 10 + 0x80096e, d2 = (0x800a9c). Queue 1: cmpi.b #0xa,(a1), entry = count++ x 10 + 0x800a36, d2 = (0x800a9e). Then 0x1ff04 move.w (0x14,a7),(a2) PGN; 0x1ff0a (0x18,a7) / 10 + d2 -> (4,a2) next tick; 0x1ff1c (0x16,a7) / 10 -> (2,a2) interval; 0x1ff2a move.l (0x1a,a7),(6,a2) builder; clr.b d0. CM848 0x538c8c: cmpwi r3,0; lbz count / cmpwi 20 (queue 1: 10) / li r3,1; mulli x 10 + 0x3fd2e2 (0x3fd3aa); stb count + 1; lhz tick; sth r4,0(r3) PGN; divw r6 / 10 + tick -> sth 4; divw r5 / 10 -> sth 2; stw r7,6; li r3,0. These are the same steps in the same order with the same constants (20 / 10 caps, 10-byte entries, divide by 10). The only difference: CM550 tests queue == 1 explicitly (another number falls through to the stores) where CM848 takes queue 1 for any non-zero value, and every caller passes 0 or 1. The same call graph position: mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink has movea.l #0x1fe84,a4 at 0x28b8a and 19 jsr (a4) calls at 0x28c6e-0x28e14 after the transmit buffer initializers; CM848 cm848_j1939_system_init makes 19 calls in the same place. 15 argument sets (queue, PGN, interval, offset) are identical and in the same order, e.g. (0, 65265, 100, 70) and (0, 61444, 20, 0) with builder 0x32c76 = sendPgn61444ElectronicEngineController1Message (a shared twin name). CM550 differs on 61443 (50 ms vs 20) and 65247 (250 ms vs 50) and has 65266 / 65252 where CM848 has 65241 / 65504. abs_refs finds no other reference and pc_relative_calls.py finds no bsr. The CM848 row 0x538c8c changes to the same name. The FUN_0001fe84(0,100) call sites need a function_definitions row: queue uint (move.l 0x10) / pgn ushort / interval_milliseconds ushort / first_send_offset_milliseconds ushort / builder dword (move.l 0x1a); return byte.

functions.role: Fills bytes 1-4 of the PGN 65252 Shutdown (SHUTDN) payload from the idle shutdown state, the idle shutdown enable bit, the A/C pressure switch and the wait to start lamp command, then sends j1939_pgn65252_tx_message.
functions.discriminator: It is the only writer of payload bytes 1-4 (0x8035f6-0x8035f9) and the only sender of j1939_pgn65252_tx_message. 0x33dfa only builds the descriptor and fills bytes 5-8.
functions.plate_comment: Builds and sends the ECM's SHUTDN broadcast (PGN 65252: every 1000 ms from 110 ms on queue 0, and the PGN 59904 request responder for 65252). Byte 1 comes from idle_shutdown_state: RESET 0x00 / COUNT 0x40 (SPN 590 timer active) / WARNING 0x44 (plus the SPN 594 driver alert) / DELAY unchanged / OVERRIDE 0x10 (SPN 592) / SHUTDOWN 0x01 (SPN 593). Byte 2 is 0x7f or 0x3f from algorithm_enable_flags_3_cal.idle_shutdown_enable (SPN 591 timer function), byte 3 is 0xfd or 0xfc from bit 0 of 0x80bcd7 (e2m 000E +9 DSAKPRSW; SPN 985 A/C high pressure fan switch), and byte 4 is 0xfd or 0xfc from bit 0 of the lamp driver command byte 0x80bcf6 (LCWTSRLP; SPN 1081 wait to start lamp). It sends j1939_pgn65252_tx_message with cm550_sendCanMessage; CM848 receives PGN 65252 but does not send it (no row before; PR #53 round 94)
functions.evidence: 0x33d38-0x33df8: a0 = a1 = 0x8035f6 (the payload; 0x33dfa sets it as the data_pointer). move.w (0x80d674) idle_shutdown_state / ext.l / cmp 5 / bhi; the jump table at 0x33d5a = 000c 0010 0016 0026 001c 0022 goes to 0x33d66 clr.b / 0x33d6a 0x40 / 0x33d70 0x44 / 0x33d80 (state 3: no store) / 0x33d76 0x10 / 0x33d7c 0x01. 0x33d80: move.w (0x803c9a) & 2 -> (1,a1) 0x7f else 0x3f. 0x33d9a: move.b (0x80bcd7) & 1 -> (2,a1) 0xfd else 0xfc. 0x33dc2: move.b (0x80bcf6) & 1 -> (3,a1) 0xfd else 0xfc. Then pea 0x8035e8 (j1939_pgn65252_tx_message) / jsr 0x104e8 cm550_sendCanMessage. It is reached through pointers only: pea 0x33d38 at 0x28d2e in mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink (scheduleJ1939PeriodicMessage(0, 0xfee4 = 65252, 1000, 110)), and pea 0x33d38 / move.w #0xfee4 / jsr (a2 = 0x2f47e) at 0x2f586 in 0x2f538, the PGN request responder registrations (its CM848 counterpart cm848_initJ1939ProtocolHandlers registers 65261 / 65263 / 65264 / 65269 / 65270 / 65271 / 65504, not 65252). abs_refs finds no other reference. CM848 has no 0xfee4 transmitter, only registerJ1939ReceiveHandler(0xfee4, receivePgn65252ShutdownMessage), so this is standalone. SHUTDN layout: byte 1 SPNs 593 / 594 / 592 / 590, byte 2 SPN 591, byte 3 SPN 985 / 875 / 605, byte 4 SPN 1081 (the j1939 MongoDB order; CM848's receive handler reads byte 3 bits 1-2 as the A/C high pressure fan switch). The IDLE_SHUTDOWN_STATE member comments already give these byte 1 values. 0x80bcf6 bit 0 = e2m 000E +28 LCWTSRLP / LCLP01EA / DSLP1. The CM848 builders that send and answer requests are named cm848_buildPgn<N><Name>Message (e.g. cm848_buildPgn65269AmbientConditionsMessage).

functions.role: At start-up, builds the PGN 65252 transmit descriptor j1939_pgn65252_tx_message (CAN ID 0xfee400 with the JCISSHPZ priority and the engine source address, 8 bytes at 0x8035f6, status 0x8035fe) and sets payload bytes 5-8 to 0xff.
functions.discriminator: It writes only the descriptor and payload bytes 5-8 and is called once. It does not send (cm550_buildPgn65252ShutdownMessage sends), and nothing in it reads engine hours or touches the VP44.
functions.plate_comment: Builds the transmit descriptor of SHUTDN (header 0xfee400: PGN 65252 Shutdown): the priority from the word 0x803f78 (e2m 1254 +2A JCISSHPZ) & 7 in the top byte and j1939_engine_node_source_address in the low byte, data length 8, data pointer 0x8035f6 and status pointer j1939_pgn65252_transmit_status, then payload bytes 5-8 = 0xff (not available). mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink calls it once, and cm550_buildPgn65252ShutdownMessage later fills bytes 1-4 and sends the message. Nothing in it concerns engine hours or the VP44 (was vp44_engineHoursPGN_65252_Builder; PR #53 round 94)
functions.evidence: 0x33dfa-0x33e56: a1 = 0x8035f6, a0 = 0x8035e8; move.l #0xfee400,(0x8035e8); move.w (0x803f78) & 7 / lsl.l #2 / andi.b #0xe3,(a0) / or.b d0,(a0); move.w #8,(4,a0); move.l a1,(6,a0); move.l #0x8035fe,(0xa,a0); move.b (0x80da01),(3,a0); move.b #0xff,(4..7,a1) = 0x8035fa-0x8035fd; rts (no send). Its one caller is jsr 0x33dfa at 0x28c30 in mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink, the 15th of the 21 buffer initializers. The e2m tool gives 1254 +002A JCISSHPZ 'DEFAULT NETWORK PRIORITY FOR IDLE SHUTDOWN MESSAGE' -> 0x803f78. It has the same shape as the CM848 descriptor builders cm848_initializePgn<N><Name>Buffer (e.g. 0x26efc for PGN 65279). CM848 has no PGN 65252 transmitter, so this is standalone; it does not touch the pump, so the prefix is cm550_.

functions.role: Every 20 ms, looks up the maximum torque map at engine_rpm_primary and alpha_blend_factor and stores the result, at least 1, as the maximum torque at the current engine speed (MTMPRPFL).
functions.discriminator: It is the only function that writes maximum_torque_map_lookup's inputs (x_input = engine speed, y_input = alpha) and calls cm550_tableLookup2D with that record. Its output 0x80db1a is the divisor in cm550_FUN_0001c0d4's torque-to-fueling scaling. 0x26a2e only fills the record pointers and seeds 0x80db1a.
functions.plate_comment: Looks up the maximum torque map (e2m 1460 MTTQMPZA over 140E MTTQMPXA engine speed and 1447 MTTQMPYA alpha) through maximum_torque_map_lookup with engine_rpm_primary and alpha_blend_factor. It stores the result, at least 1, as the maximum torque at the current engine speed 0x80db1a (e2m 1461 +0 MTMPRPFL, ft-lb). Called last in cm550_runEvery4FramesTaskSetPhase0 (every 20 ms); cm550_FUN_0001c0d4 divides the torque derate limit by it. CM848's counterpart is 0x29c98 (cm848_calculateFuelDemandFilter: three lookups of the same map blended by chi) (was cm550_FUN_000269f2; PR #53 round 94)
functions.evidence: 0x269f2-0x26a2c: a2 = 0x80db1a, a3 = 0x801a94 (maximum_torque_map_lookup); move.w (0x80ccf6 engine_rpm_primary),(6,a3) x_input; move.w (0x80a8f8 alpha_blend_factor),(0xe,a3) y_input; jsr 0x35088 cm550_tableLookup2D; move.w d0,(a2); cmpi.w #1 / bcc / move.w #1,(a2). It is the last call of cm550_runEvery4FramesTaskSetPhase0 (0x1b518). e2m tool: 1461 +0000 MTMPRPFL 'MAX TORQUE AT CURRENT RPM IN FOOT-POUNDS' -> 0x80db1a; 104A +0000 ALPHA -> 0x80a8f8; 100C +0004 ENGRPM -> 0x80ccf6. The other reader of 0x80db1a is cm550_FUN_0001c0d4 (0x1c0da; the divisor of cm550_scaleByRatioSigned). CM848 0x29c98 (called by cm848_periodicTaskSet_sensorProcessing) makes three cm848_dualAxisTableInterpolation calls of the same MTTQMPZA map (alpha 0 row, chi lower, chi upper) at the filtered engine speed and blends them with cm848_interpolateAlphaChiValue into fuel_demand_filter_dimension (0x40aee6; 0 -> 1). The role is the same but the code differs, so this is a counterpart.

functions.role: At start-up, seeds the maximum torque at the current engine speed (0x80db1a) with 1 and points maximum_torque_map_lookup at the MTTQMPXA / MTTQMPYA axes (axis offsets 2) and the MTTQMPZA grid.
functions.discriminator: It writes the record's three pointers and two axis offsets, no input and no lookup, and is called once from mc68k_applicationMain. 0x269f2 writes the inputs and looks the map up.
functions.plate_comment: Start-up (mc68k_applicationMain): seeds the maximum torque at the current engine speed 0x80db1a (MTMPRPFL) with 1 and points maximum_torque_map_lookup at its tables: x axis 0x808346 (MTTQMPXA) and y axis 0x808372 (MTTQMPYA), each with axis offset 2, and the grid 0x80837c (MTTQMPZA). cm550_calculateMaximumTorqueAtCurrentEngineSpeed then looks it up every 20 ms. CM848's counterpart is 0x29de0 (cm848_initFuelDemandFilterDimensions: the result 1 and three lookup caches 2) (was cm550_FUN_00026a2e; PR #53 round 94)
functions.evidence: 0x26a2e-0x26a62: a0 = 0x801a94; move.w #1,(0x80db1a); move.l #0x808346,(2,a0); move.w #2,(0x801a94); move.l #0x808372,(0xa,a0); move.w #2,(8,a0); move.l #0x80837c,(0x10,a0); rts. Called once from mc68k_applicationMain, right after the 0x8970 progress marker store. The record's rows (maximum_torque_map_lookup, maximum_torque_map_x_axis / _y_axis / _grid) were typed in round 94 stage C. CM848 0x29de0 (called from cm848_applicationMain) sets fuel_demand_filter_dimension = 1 and the three maximum_torque_map_*_cached_axis_offsets = 2. CM848 has no record pointers, so this is a counterpart.

functions.role: At start-up, points injection_timing_misfire_limit_lookup at the misfire limit table's engine speed and boost axes (axis offsets 2) and grid, and clears the timing before the misfire limit (BSTABELM) and the misfire timing limit (BSTAMNLM).
functions.discriminator: It is the only writer of the misfire lookup record's pointers and offsets, and it clears both 818E words. It runs once at start-up; 0x26ab8 computes the limit and cm550_applyMisfireTimingLimit applies it. Nothing in it concerns a fuel demand.
functions.plate_comment: Start-up (mc68k_applicationMain): points injection_timing_misfire_limit_lookup at the misfire limit table: y axis 0x807944 (8190 BSTAESYA engine speed) and x axis 0x80793a (818F BSTABSXA boost pressure), each with axis offset 2, and the grid 0x80794e (8191 BSTATBZA). It then clears injection_timing_before_misfire_limit (818E +2 BSTABELM) and the misfire timing limit 0x80a26e (818E +0 BSTAMNLM). CM848's counterpart is 0x29e24 (cm848_initProtectionFilterAccumulators: the cache offsets 2 and the same two clears in the same order) (was cm550_fuelDemandTablePointersInit; PR #53 round 94)
functions.evidence: 0x26a7e-0x26ab6: a0 = 0x801aaa; move.w #2,(8,a0); move.l #0x807944,(0xa,a0); move.w #2,(0x801aaa); move.l #0x80793a,(2,a0); move.l #0x80794e,(0x10,a0); clr.w (0x80a270); clr.w (0x80a26e). Called once from mc68k_applicationMain, after the 0x8918 marker. e2m tool: 818E +0002 BSTABELM -> 0x80a270, 818E +0000 BSTAMNLM -> 0x80a26e. CM848 0x29e24 (cm848_applicationMain) sets injection_timing_main_misfire_limit_cached_axis_offsets[1] = 2 and [0] = 2, then clears 0x40aeea (e2m 8A3D +2 SOI_Before_MST, misnamed injection_timing_pid_init_flag) and 0x40aee8 (8A3D +0 Misfire_Timing_Limit). The order is the same (y then x, the before-limit value then the limit), but CM550 also stores the three table pointers, so this is a counterpart, not a twin.

functions.role: While misfire_timing_limit_enable is set, looks up the misfire timing limit table at boost pressure and engine_rpm_primary and stores the result as the misfire timing limit (BSTAMNLM).
functions.discriminator: It is the only periodic writer of 0x80a26e. cm550_applyMisfireTimingLimit reads the same enable bit, but it only compares fuel_timing_advance_value with 0x80a26e and raises the timing.
functions.plate_comment: While algorithm_enable_flags_32_cal.misfire_timing_limit_enable (e2m BSTALMEN) is set, looks up the misfire timing limit table (8191 BSTATBZA, the minimum advance for misfire) through injection_timing_misfire_limit_lookup with boost pressure 0x80a320 (1004 +76 BSTPRS) and engine_rpm_primary. The result goes to the misfire timing limit 0x80a26e (818E +0 BSTAMNLM), and cm550_applyMisfireTimingLimit raises the timing to it. Called in cm550_runEvery4FramesTaskSetPhase2 (every 20 ms). CM848's counterpart is cm848_calculateInjectionTimingMainMisfireLimit (0x29e50) (was cm550_rpmLoadParameterLookup; PR #53 round 94)
functions.evidence: 0x26ab8-0x26aee: a2 = 0x801aaa; move.w (0x803cd4) & 1 (algorithm_enable_flags_32_cal.misfire_timing_limit_enable) / beq skip; move.w (0x80a320),(6,a2) x = boost pressure (e2m 1004 +0076 BSTPRS; boost_pressure_sensor_state.filtered_value in the decompile); move.w (0x80ccf6),(0xe,a2) y = engine_rpm_primary; jsr 0x35088 cm550_tableLookup2D; move.w d0,(0x80a26e). It is the 6th call of cm550_runEvery4FramesTaskSetPhase2 (0x1b5ce). cm550_applyMisfireTimingLimit (0x26af0) reads 0x80a26e at 0x26b02. CM848 0x29e50 (cm848_periodicTaskSet_auxiliaryControl) has the same enable role (algorithm_enable_flags_40_cal.misfire_timing_limit_enable) and the same axes (boost pressure x filtered engine speed), and it writes the 8A40 table result into 8A3D +0 Misfire_Timing_Limit. But it makes a direct cm848_dualAxisTableInterpolation call with cm848_calculateBoostPressure() as x, so this is a counterpart. The code computes no load and reads no parameter, so the old name is wrong.

globals.comment: ETC1 (PGN 61442) byte 1 as received: bits 1-2 driveline engaged (SPN 560) and bits 5-6 shift in process (SPN 574). The ETC1 receive handler 0x2efd0 (registered for 0xf002 at 0x2f114) stores data[0] here for an 8-byte frame from j1939_transmission_source_address (any source when that is 0xff). When both fields are 0 it sets the driveline disengaged (out of gear) flag and timer. CM848's j1939_powertrain_messages_received.etc1_status_byte_1. It is not a TSC1 byte (was tsc1_message_byte_0; PR #53 round 94)
globals.evidence: 0x2efde movea.l #0x801d44,a1; 0x2f010 move.b (a0),(a1) with a0 = the frame's data pointer (+6); reads move.b (a1) at 0x2f0ca (& 0x30) and 0x2f0d4 (& 3). abs_refs finds only the movea at 0x2efde. 0x2f114: pea 0x2efd0 / move.w #0xf002 / jsr 0x21272 registerJ1939ReceiveHandler. CM848 cm848_j1939ProcessPgn61442Etc1 stores *rx_msg->data_pointer to etc1_status_byte_1 and runs the same & 0x30 == 0 and & 3 == 0 test for its out of gear flag.

globals.comment: ETC1 (PGN 61442) byte 5 as received. Bits 1-2 are the engine momentary overspeed enable (SPN 606): 1 starts the high idle override when tsc1_override_control_mode is 1 and the controlling device is the transmission, and a value other than 1 or 3 clears it. Bits 3-4 are the progressive shift disable (SPN 607): 1 sets progressive_shift_disable_flag and its timer. The ETC1 receive handler 0x2efd0 stores data[4] here. CM848's j1939_powertrain_messages_received.etc1_status_byte_5 (was tsc1_message_control_byte; PR #53 round 94)
globals.evidence: 0x2f012-0x2f022: move.b (4,data),d0; movea.l #0x801d48,a0 (a2 = a0); move.b d0,(a0). Reads move.b (a2) at 0x2f02c (& 3 == 1), 0x2f062 (& 3 != 3), 0x2f08a (& 0xc == 4) and 0x2f0b0 (& 0xc != 0xc). abs_refs finds only the movea at 0x2f01a. CM848: etc1_status_byte_5 = rx_msg->data_pointer[4] with the same & 3 == 1 and & 0xc == 4 tests.

globals.comment: TSC1 (PGN 0) byte 1 as received by processEngineTsc1Request: bits 1-2 override control mode (SPN 695), bits 3-4 requested speed control conditions (SPN 696) and bits 5-6 override control mode priority (SPN 897). CM848's j1939_powertrain_messages_received.tsc1_control_byte (was torque_control_message_byte_0; PR #53 round 94)
globals.evidence: processEngineTsc1Request (the verified twin of CM848's): 0x2f130 movea.l #0x801d4c,a3; 0x2f150 move.b (data),(0x801d4c); 0x2f156 & 3 -> d3 (mode); 0x2f160 & 0x30 -> d4 (priority); 0x2f292 / 0x2f33e reads (byte_indicating_engine_commands..., & 0xc >> 2 = the speed control condition). Byte accesses only.

globals.comment: TSC1 bytes 2-3, the requested speed / speed limit (SPN 898, 0.125 rpm), kept big-endian: [0] = data[2] (the high byte) and [1] = data[1] (the low byte). processEngineTsc1Request rebuilds the word as [0] << 8 | [1] for modes 1 and 3. Byte accesses only (odd address). CM848's j1939_powertrain_messages_received.tsc1_requested_speed (PR #53 round 94)
globals.evidence: 0x2f16e move.b (1,data),(2,a3) -> 0x801d4e; 0x2f178 move.b (2,data),(1,a3) -> 0x801d4d (a3 = 0x801d4c). 0x2f232-0x2f238 and 0x2f316-0x2f31c: move.b (1,a3) / lsl.w #8 / move.b (2,a3) -> the word that is compared with or stored to 0x801d56. Decompile: CONCAT11(DAT_00801d4d,DAT_00801d4e). No absolute reference to 0x801d4d or 0x801d4e and no row today.

globals.comment: TSC1 byte 4, the requested torque / torque limit (SPN 518, percent + 125) as received. processEngineTsc1Request turns it into the datalink torque demand fueling (mode 2) or the torque limit fueling (mode 3). CM848's j1939_powertrain_messages_received.tsc1_requested_torque (was torque_control_percent_byte; PR #53 round 94)
globals.evidence: processEngineTsc1Request 0x2f17e: move.b (3,data),(3,a3) -> 0x801d4f; read at 0x2f218 and 0x2f226 (cmp.b against 0x801d58) and as d2 = (3,a3) for the stores at 0x2f388 and 0x2f42c; decompile: (ushort)torque_control_percent_byte * 0x100 - 32000.

globals.comment: The priority bits (TSC1 byte 1 & 0x30, SPN 897) of the accepted engine request. While a J1939 request from another source is active, a new request with a higher priority value is rejected. At the same priority, only a mode 3 request can take over an active mode 3 request, and only with a lower torque or speed. CM848's j1939_powertrain_messages_received.tsc1_accepted_priority (PR #53 round 94)
globals.evidence: processEngineTsc1Request: 0x2f1f2 cmp.b (0x801d54),d4 / bhi reject; 0x2f1fc cmp.b (0x801d54),d4 / bne; 0x2f29e move.b d4,(0x801d54) after acceptance (decompile: DAT_00801d54 = bVar2 with bVar2 = byte 1 & 0x30). Byte accesses only; no row today.

globals.comment: The requested speed (0.125 rpm) of the accepted speed control request (mode 1) or speed / torque limit request (mode 3). A mode 3 takeover at the same priority with an equal torque needs a lower speed. CM848's j1939_powertrain_messages_received.tsc1_accepted_requested_speed (PR #53 round 94)
globals.evidence: 0x2f22c move.w (0x801d56).l,d0 is compared with the new request's speed (bls rejects it); 0x2f320 (mode 1) and 0x2f41c (mode 3) store d0 = (1,a3) << 8 | (2,a3) with move.w d0,(0x801d56). Word accesses only; no row today (decompile _DAT_00801d56).

globals.comment: The requested torque (percent + 125) of the accepted torque control request (mode 2) or limit request (mode 3). A mode 3 takeover at the same priority needs a lower torque. CM848's j1939_powertrain_messages_received.tsc1_accepted_requested_torque (PR #53 round 94)
globals.evidence: 0x2f212 and 0x2f220: move.b (0x801d58),d0 / cmp.b (3,a3),d0 (bcs rejects, bne takes over). 0x2f388 and 0x2f42c: move.b d2,(0x801d58) with d2 = (3,a3), the mode 2 and mode 3 paths. Byte accesses only; no row today.

roles.role: Adds one periodic J1939 broadcast to a transmit queue. The queue argument selects the queue: 0 = engine node queue (entries at 0x80096e, count byte 0x800a9a, full at 20, tick 0x800a9c), 1 = retarder node queue (entries at 0x800a36, count 0x800a9b, full at 10, tick 0x800a9e). It writes the next 10-byte j1939_periodic_transmit_entry_t in this order: +0 PGN, +4 next_tick = offset ms / 10 + current tick, +2 interval_ticks = interval ms / 10, +6 builder address. It returns 1 when the queue is full, else 0. The only reference is movea.l #0x1fe84,a4 at 0x28b8a (operand at 0x28b8c) in mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink, which then makes 19 jsr (a4) calls. Each call pushes a long queue, a word PGN, a word interval ms, a word offset ms and a long builder: (0,65265,100,70,0x31c84) (0,61444,20,0,0x32c76) (0,61443,50,10) (0,65247,250,30) (0,65251,5000,110) (1,61440,100,50) (0,65266,100,90) (1,65249,5000,301) (0,65262,1000,430) (0,65252,1000,110,0x33d38) (0,65263,500,130) (0,65264,100,150) (0,65269,1000,170) (0,65270,500,190) (0,65271,1000,210) (0,65226,1000,500) (0,65213,1000,50) (0,61441,100,20) (0,65279,10000,40). The RAM dump holds exactly these 17 + 2 entries. For the new row, the prototype in 2-byte stack slots is: dword queue @+4, word pgn @+8, word interval_milliseconds @+0xa, word first_send_offset_milliseconds @+0xc, pointer builder @+0xe; returns byte.

roles.role: Builds and sends PGN 65252 Shutdown (SHUTDN). It fills the payload at 0x8035f6 (the data of j1939_pgn65252_tx_message). Byte 1 comes from idle_shutdown_state (0x80d674) through the jump table at 0x33d5a: 0->0x00, 1->0x40, 2->0x44, 3->unchanged, 4->0x10, 5->0x01, above 5 unchanged. These are the SPN 593/594/592/590 two-bit fields. Byte 2 = 0x7f when algorithm_enable_flags_3_cal.idle_shutdown_enable (0x803c9a & 2) is set, else 0x3f: SPN 591, enabled or disabled in calibration. Byte 3 = 0xfd when 0x80bcd7 bit 0 is set (e2m 000E +9 DSAKPRSW, software value of the air conditioner pressure switch), else 0xfc: SPN 985. Byte 4 = 0xfd when 0x80bcf6 bit 0 is set, else 0xfc: SPN 1081 engine wait to start lamp. 0x80bcf6 bit 0 is the wait to start lamp output (cm550_iahDisableWaitToStartLamp clears it with andi.b #0xfe). It then calls cm550_sendCanMessage(&j1939_pgn65252_tx_message). Two paths reach it: (1) the periodic entry queue 0, PGN 65252, every 1000 ms from 110 ms (pea 0x33d38 at 0x28d2e); (2) the PGN request responder table, through 0x2f538 calling 0x2f47e(0xfee4, 0x33d38) at 0x2f586. 0x2f47e adds a {PGN, handler} entry to 0x801d5a, and 0x2f4be, the PGN 59904 request handler, walks that table.

roles.role: (Extra: it is the function that stores 0x801d44 / 0x801d48.) This is the J1939 PGN 61442 ETC1 receive handler: 0x2f114 (cm550_systemControlFunction3) calls registerJ1939ReceiveHandler(0xf002, 0x2efd0). It accepts only 8-byte frames from _j1939_transmission_source_address (ROM 0x60f82; 0xff = any sender). Byte 1 goes to 0x801d44 and byte 5 to 0x801d48. Byte 5 bits 1-2 = 1 (SPN 606, engine momentary overspeed enable) with tsc1_override_control_mode = 1 and engine_control_device_indicator = 1 sets high_idle_override_active_flag (JCHII1OD) and its timeout timer (JCEGOSTM + 1). A value other than 1 or 3 clears them. While the recovery flag 0x80da98 is set, the timer is reloaded with JCTMRCTM + 1 instead. Byte 5 bits 3-4 = 1 (SPN 607) sets progressive_shift_disable_flag (JCPSDB) and its timer (JCPSTM + 1); a value other than 3 clears them. Byte 1 bits 1-2 = 0 with bits 5-6 = 0 (driveline disengaged, no shift in process) sets driveline_disengaged_flag (JCOG), its timer (JCDRDITM + 1) and out_of_gear_network_type = 1 (J1939); otherwise it clears them.

roles.role: The whole e2m DGFUIDEN record: F +570, 'bit mapped parameter used to disable/enable the processing of a particular fault'. Block F is RAM 0x80654c (parameter ID table: DG00ELTM / FLT_DATA). The type is B and the length 38 decimal = 19 words, 0x806abc-0x806ae1. It ends exactly where block 1003's first record starts (0x806ae2, intake_manifold_temperature_sensor_config), which proves the length is decimal; it is the last record of block F, and every family e2m gives it 38. It is indexed like the 32 fault status words at 0x806000 (SSERSSnn): fault n is word n >> 4, bit n & 15. Every reader ANDs a status bit with the same bit here. Examples: 0xe9ce tests 0x806002 & 0x400 with 0x806abe & 0x400; 0x1e490 tests 0x80600e & 4 with 0x806aca & 4; 0x16ef6 tests 0x806006 with (0x6,a2). Other readers use it as the gate to set or log a fault: 0x115b2 sets status word 0 bit 12 only while this bit is set, and cm550_processFaultScanGroup (0x14900) logs a fault only when its bit is set. Every access in the dumped ROM is a read: absolute, base + 2/4/6/8/0xc, and the indexed move.w (0,a0,d0.w*2) with d0 = fault number >> 4. The dump contents (fc00 2600 d007 006b 2b3f f800 b7ee 0200 ea00 0299 0040 0000 x5 f800 f7bf 0efb) appear in neither the ROM nor the EEPROM dump. So the record is set from outside the dumped code (a tool write, or code above 0x40000). It is outside the EEPROM mirror, so no _cal.
